codes.evidence_quote: Desde el punto de vista total, el flamenco de verdad se vio seriamente disminuido por la muerte de cada uno de ellos.
codes.target: the flamenco associated with Fernandillo, Diego del Gastor, María and related older artists
codes.rationale: The passage explicitly identifies a valued form as 'flamenco de verdad', authorizing those artists as bearers of real flamenco.

codes.evidence_quote: pronto este arte se quedará completamente en manos de los profesionales astutos, un espectáculo teatral sin alma ni significado
codes.rationale: The text frames staged professional spectacle as a soulless degradation of real flamenco.

codes.evidence_quote: No quedan muchos de los auténticos flamencos
codes.target: the named older artists and their philosophy of flamenco
codes.rationale: The passage canonizes a small group of older figures as among the remaining authentic flamencos whose deaths diminish the art.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The article evokes fiesta and lived sociability, but the visible excerpt does not clearly contrast participatory settings with spectatorship as a distinct discourse function beyond the anti-theatrical authenticity claim.

derived_analysis.target: older intimate flamenco associated with Fernandillo and the Morón milieu, contrasted with professional theatrical flamenco

annotation_notes: Truncated article, but the visible ending gives clear authenticity and anti-spectacle evidence.

codes.evidence_quote: un flamencólogo es un señor que escribe relativamente bien, tiene poder en el mundo del flamenco, ha escrito algún que otro libro, pero que adolece de un desconocimiento enorme de nuestros cantes
codes.rationale: The author directly contests expert/flamencologist authority by accusing it of power without cante knowledge.

codes.evidence_quote: Sólo me siento un aficionado que llega al mundo de la literatura y de la crítica desde lo más jondo de nuestros cantes y sus vivencias y no al contrario.
codes.target: aficionado knowledge grounded in cante and lived experience
codes.rationale: The passage draws an epistemic boundary between insider aficionado knowledge rooted in lived flamenco and outside literary criticism.

codes.evidence_quote: Diferenciamos el decir el cante con el saber cantar. Saber cantar es relativamente fácil... Pero la dificultad donde se genera, es en el decir.
codes.rationale: The passage defines flamenco quality through the aesthetic criterion of 'decir el cante' rather than merely singing well.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The text mentions vivencias and accumulated experience, but it does not clearly describe oral, embodied, familial, or lineage transmission as the mechanism of learning.

derived_analysis.target: authority to define and judge contemporary flamenco

annotation_notes: The visible excerpt is polemical and clearly contests who has authority to speak about flamenco.

codes.evidence_quote: Entonces, tu baile se forma de lo aprendido de las familias. —¡Claro, como se bailaba antes!
codes.rationale: The passage explicitly frames her learning as family/community-based transmission rather than formal schooling.

codes.evidence_quote: conviviendo con personas y con familias de una estirpe fuera de serie, como la de los "Pelúos", los "Amador"... Todo eso lo he vivido y me ha llenado de arte

codes.rationale: Community, family lineage, and convivencia are presented as the social ground that authorizes and fills her art.

codes.rationale: The text grounds value in roots and proximity to the base, contrasting it with a present loss of rootedness.
